haiku-low.q1: The API compares reports.row_count (unfiltered) with 10,000. At or below 10,000, the CSV streams directly as the click's response. Above it, the API returns 202 with export_id and status, and the link is emailed later.
haiku-low.q2: A unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running blocks the insert. The API returns that existing export with 200 and starts nothing.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link works for 24 hours from the email. The bucket's existing lifecycle rule deletes the file 7 days after creation. No cleanup job exists.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, with waits of 60 s then 300 s. After the last failure, on_final_failure sets status failed, stores the error, and emails the user. The page shows failed.
haiku-low.q5: Only the read replica. Export paths never read report rows from the primary.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports table's status column. The page calls GET exports/latest on load and after a click, and polls every 5 seconds while queued or running, so a reopened page shows current state.
haiku-low.q7: It reads keyset batches from the replica, appends CSV to an about 8 MB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part, then frees it. Only one buffer and one batch are in memory at a time.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing is visible at the key until complete_multipart, and a failed attempt aborts its upload. A dead worker's stale upload is discarded after 24 hours. The next attempt restarts from the first row with a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: The filters and cols are copied into the query column of the report_exports row at click time. The job payload holds only export_id, so the job reads the query from the row.
haiku-low.q10: The database unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The second concurrent insert hits it, and the API returns the existing export.
haiku-low.q11: complete_multipart must succeed and status must be set to done with the key stored, before the email. If the queue reruns after done, the job sees done and stops, so no second file or email.
haiku-low.q12: The request errors and no state is created, so nothing needs cleanup. The user clicks again.

sonnet.q1: The API reads reports.row_count (unfiltered total) and compares it with 10,000. At 10,000 rows or fewer (small): the response to the click is the CSV itself (header row plus rows streamed from the replica); no record, job or storage. Above 10,000 (large): a report_exports row is created, a report_export job is enqueued, and the API returns 202 with {export_id, status}; the CSV is built in the background, stored in object storage, and a download link is emailed.
sonnet.q2: The unique index on (user_id, report_id) for queued/running rows is hit, so the API returns the existing active export with 200 and starts nothing new. This holds whatever the filters. A new export is allowed once the earlier one is done or failed.
sonnet.q3: The signed link is valid for 24 hours (86,400 s) from the email. The file is removed by the exports bucket's existing lifecycle rule 7 days after creation; no cleanup job is built.
sonnet.q4: 3 attempts in total (waits of 60 s then 300 s between). After the last fails, on_final_failure is called once: it sets status failed, stores the error, and emails the user that the export failed. The page then shows failed.
sonnet.q5: Only the read replica (never the primary), in keyset batches, for both the small and large paths.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports table (status column: queued/running/done/failed). The page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load and after a click to get the user's newest export (which also gives the export_id after a reload), and polls every 5 seconds while it is queued or running.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads keyset batches from the replica after the last row_id, appends CSV text to a buffer of about 8 MB, uploads each full buffer as a multipart part and frees it. At most one buffer and one batch are in memory (about 110 parts for 900 MB, under the 10,000-part limit). Then complete_multipart. Whether it fits in the 30-minute timeout is an open question needing measurement.
sonnet.q8: The failing attempt aborts its multipart upload; if the worker died, the bucket discards the stale upload after 24 hours. Nothing is visible at the key until complete_multipart, so partial data is never downloadable. The next attempt (retry) restarts from the first row, reusing the same export record and key, with a new upload; status stays running.
sonnet.q9: They are copied from the page URL by the click into the query column of the report_exports row. The job payload contains only the export_id, so the job reads the query from that row.
sonnet.q10: The unique index on report_exports (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. The insert that loses hits the index and the API returns the existing export with 200.
sonnet.q11: complete_multipart must have succeeded and status must be set to done with the key stored; only then is the email sent via send_email with a signed_url link. If the job runs again after success, step 5 sees the export is already done and stops, so no second file or email.
sonnet.q12: The request errors; there is no record, job or stored state to clean up, and the user clicks again.
